differences.title: 1. COMMUNICATION DIRECTION
differences.leftDesc: Efficient for real-time updates pushed from server without client request.
differences.rightDesc: Enables full-duplex communication for interactive, real-time applications.

differences.title: 2. CONNECTION TYPE
differences.leftDesc: Leverages existing HTTP infrastructure, simpler to implement and proxy.
differences.rightDesc: Maintains persistent, independent connection for constant data flow.

differences.title: 3. LATENCY
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for scenarios where server needs to push data frequently.
differences.rightDesc: Extremely low latency for instant message exchange.

differences.title: 4. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Best for news feeds, stock tickers, notifications, live scores.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for gaming, collaborative tools, real-time chat.

differences.title: 5. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Built on HTTP, often requires less complex server-side logic.
differences.rightDesc: Requires dedicated WebSocket server, potentially more state management.

differences.title: 6. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: HTTP benefits like load balancing and caching are more straightforward.
differences.rightDesc: Managing many persistent connections can be resource-intensive.

differences.title: 7. BROWSER SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Modern browsers support Server-Sent Events via EventSource API.
differences.rightDesc: Universally supported by all modern web browsers.
